conclusions: All sixteen live Super calls delivered complete JSON with known logical and physical usage; no provider failure, retry, truncation or local delivery block was observed.

Both arms attempted all four cases and accepted none. Native-format rejection fell from three control proposals to one treatment proposal; treatment constructed seven native proposals versus five control. This narrower emission signal is supporting reliability, not cognitive improvement.

Treatment had four certificate-schema rejections, all on interpolation stages, and three mathematically incorrect proposals. Control had five mathematically incorrect proposals. Schema-invalid certificates were not mathematically graded; their reasoning correctness is unknown.

Six unique stages were mathematically graded and wrong; two treatment stages were schema-only and ungraded. All eight stages reached the acceptance callback. The frozen report's graded counters include certificate-schema rejection and must not be misread as eight reasoning grades.

Treatment used 35676 reported tokens versus 40545 control, with the same eight logical and eight physical calls per arm. All four pairs used no more treatment model compute, but none met the five-percent realized-token matching tolerance.

Native rejections, certificate-schema failures and executed mathematical failures remain distinct. No missing labels, duplicate labels or incorrect equation can be identified precisely from the retained hashes alone; raw IR/certificates were deliberately not persisted.
The eight mathematical proposal failures and zero accepted solutions constrain the next mechanism. The finite expression frontend does not supply mathematics or constitute a new cognitive engine.

These are four new parameter values in two known formal families, not family-disjoint generalization, an official benchmark score or measured recursion. No default, authority or cognitive promotion is supported.
